question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping’s firm grip on the Chinese Communist Party, demonstrated through ongoing anti-corruption purges that have removed senior military figures such as Zhang Youxia and Liu Zhenli from the Central Military Commission as recently as August 2026, sustains trader consensus that he will remain in office through the end of 2026. These actions, which have depleted potential rival networks without visible elite pushback, align with patterns of centralized control established since term limits were lifted in 2018. The 21st Party Congress scheduled for 2027 is widely viewed as the venue for a fourth term rather than transition, with succession discussions deferred. While sudden health developments or unanticipated internal realignments remain theoretically possible, current institutional dominance and absence of organized opposition support the elevated probability assigned to continuity.
